polaris: LP29-C2: A=Srivastava-style orbital-overlap integral has absorbed the main structural explanatory power for transport/effective mass, so LP29 graph metrics are only reparameterizations; B=after controlling orbital-overlap, onsite variance, density, mobility-edge margin, batch and finite size, graph spectral features still predict external Hall/Drude/Wannier/spectral residual labels.
framework: Distributed network reliability / error-correcting redundancy: the same local channel capacity budget can produce different global reliability depending on expansion, bottlenecks, and adversarial failure response.

math_object.borrowed_structure: Capacity-weighted graph with fixed edge-weight budget but variable expansion and targeted-damage sensitivity.
math_object.translation_to_physics: Treat Srivastava-style orbital overlap as local edge capacity w_ij on an In-s/O-mediated structural graph. The overlap baseline captures the low-order capacity budget and weight distribution; lambda_2, spectral radius, and high-betweenness damage test how that capacity is organized into a percolating electronic backbone.
math_object.non_equivalence_core: A scalar overlap budget S=sum w_ij is invariant to many edge rearrangements. Weighted Laplacian connectivity lambda_2, adjacency spectral radius rho(A), and high-betweenness attack loss are not invariant, because they depend on bottleneck placement, backbone redundancy, and eigenmode support.

findings: B's viable attack is not to assert that graph metrics are automatically new physics. The testable claim is narrower: after nuisance-orthogonalizing against orbital-overlap, onsite disorder, density, mobility-edge margin, finite-size, and batch controls, graph spectra must retain held-out predictive signal on external labels not generated by the graph proxy. If they fail under this residual test, LP29-C2 must be downgraded to reparameterized overlap geometry.

cross_disciplinary_jump.structure: global reliability is determined by expansion and targeted-failure response, not only by total link capacity
cross_disciplinary_jump.isomorphism: total link capacity maps to orbital-overlap scalar; expansion maps to lambda_2; dominant backbone mode maps to spectral radius/eigenvector support; adversarial link failure maps to high-betweenness defect damage
cross_disciplinary_jump.physical_prediction: Two atomistic structures with matched overlap scalar and weight histogram can have different transport residuals if one has expander-like In-s connectivity while the other routes current through narrow high-betweenness bridges.

residual_framework.unit_of_analysis: same material sample, AIMD snapshot, or seeded structural realization with all descriptors and external labels joined before modeling
external_labels: Hall mobility or conductivity with Hall-factor convention predeclared
Drude weight, optical scattering time, or plasma-frequency-derived label
Wannier/QSGW bandwidth, velocity, effective mass, or orbital-character label computed independently
spectral linewidth, IPR, ridge coherence, or level-statistics label from electronic-structure calculations
forbidden_labels: labels generated by the same graph Hamiltonian used to compute graph metrics
transport proxies algebraically derived from the tested graph score

nuisance_orthogonal_test.test: Fit Y_perp ~ M_perp with nested cross-validation, batch-preserving permutation, and leave-one-family-out validation.
nuisance_orthogonal_test.success_condition: Graph-added residual model improves held-out prediction and preserves predeclared sign relative to all null controls.

minimum_synthetic_benchmark.purpose: A minimal benchmark for testing whether the residualization and null controls can distinguish reparameterized overlap from genuinely global graph organization. It is a software/protocol benchmark, not material validation.
minimum_synthetic_benchmark.nodes: N=64 to 256 sites; multiple seeds per N.
base_graphs: degree-corrected stochastic block graph with bridge bottleneck
random geometric graph with matched density
degree-preserving rewired variants of each graph
minimum_synthetic_benchmark.edge_weights: Draw w_ij from a common overlap-like distribution, then rescale each graph so sum(w_ij), mean degree, degree sequence where applicable, and weight histogram are matched.
minimum_synthetic_benchmark.onsite_disorder: epsilon_i sampled with fixed variance sigma_epsilon^2 across paired controls.
minimum_synthetic_benchmark.baseline_scalar: S_overlap = sum_{(i,j)} w_ij plus weight moments and onsite variance.
graph_features: lambda_2 of normalized or weighted Laplacian, normalization fixed before fitting
damage_high_betweenness = relative loss of lambda_2 or effective conductance after removing top-k betweenness edges

synthetic_labels.B_positive_label: Y = beta0*S_overlap + beta1*sigma_epsilon + beta2*lambda_2 - beta3*attack_gap + noise
synthetic_labels.leakage_trap_label: Y generated from graph Hamiltonian eigenvalues and explicitly flagged as forbidden for material validation

controls: degree-preserving rewiring at fixed degree sequence and weight histogram
weight shuffling at fixed graph topology and S_overlap
matched random damage versus high-betweenness damage
batch/family labels assigned by generator and held out in leave-one-family-out tests

pass_fail.software_pass: Pipeline detects graph residual only in B_positive_label and not in A_null_label after baseline residualization.
pass_fail.control_pass: Rewired controls destroy or reduce the synthetic graph residual while preserving S_overlap.

degree_preserving_rewired_controls.construction: Use double-edge swaps preserving degree sequence; after rewiring, assign the original weight multiset by rank or random permutation, then rescale to identical S_overlap.
degree_preserving_rewired_controls.expected_if_B_true: External residual prediction should degrade when rewiring destroys bottleneck/expansion structure while preserving degree and overlap budget.
degree_preserving_rewired_controls.expected_if_A_true: Rewired and original graphs should be statistically indistinguishable once overlap scalar, weight distribution, onsite variance, density, and batch are controlled.

high_betweenness_damage.definition: Remove or downweight top-k weighted edge-betweenness edges and measure relative loss in lambda_2, effective conductance proxy, or held-out external residual prediction.
high_betweenness_damage.matched_control: Remove same total weight or same number of random edges, repeated across seeds.
high_betweenness_damage.B_direction: targeted damage loss > random damage loss; larger high-betweenness damage predicts lower Hall/Drude/Wannier/spectral residual labels after baseline controls.
high_betweenness_damage.A_direction: targeted and random damage provide no stable external residual signal beyond the overlap baseline.

lambda_2_residual.definition: lambda2_perp = (I - P_B) * lambda_2 after regressing lambda_2 on overlap scalar, onsite variance, density, mobility-edge margin, finite-size, and batch.
lambda_2_residual.prediction: lambda2_perp should be positively associated with Hall mobility, Drude weight, Wannier bandwidth/ridge coherence residuals and negatively associated with linewidth/IPR residuals.
lambda_2_residual.critical_null: If lambda2_perp is nonzero only inside synthetic graph labels or only in training batches, it is a protocol artifact.

downgrade_plan_if_overlap_absorbs_all_re.trigger: Nested residual tests show no stable held-out improvement from graph spectra; coefficients fail sign stability; degree-preserving rewired controls match original performance; external labels collapse to orbital-overlap baseline.
downgrade_plan_if_overlap_absorbs_all_re.downgraded_claim: LP29 graph metrics are a useful visualization and high-dimensional reparameterization of orbital-overlap geometry, not an independent mechanism for transport/effective mass.
salvage_value: Retain graph spectra as diagnostic compression for overlap heterogeneity and finite-size/batch QA.
Report negative result as evidence that Srivastava-style orbital-overlap integral is closer to a sufficient statistic for the tested labels.
Move C2 from mechanism claim to measurement-protocol claim: graph metrics are allowed only as null controls or visualization until external residual labels re-open the case.
downgrade_plan_if_overlap_absorbs_all_re.hard_stop: Do not reinterpret failed residual prediction as hidden graph physics without new external labels or a predeclared alternative graph observable.

strangest_prediction: At fixed orbital-overlap scalar, onsite variance, carrier density, mobility-edge margin, finite size, and batch, a small number of O-O/coordination defects placed on high-betweenness In-s backbone edges should depress external Drude weight or Hall mobility residual more than a larger total defect penalty placed in low-betweenness redundant regions.
a_objection: A will object that lambda_2, spectral radius, and betweenness are computed from overlap-derived weights, so they are only nonlinear features of the same orbital-overlap baseline and will overfit small batches.
b_response: That objection is valid unless B survives the nuisance-orthogonal residual test, degree/weight-preserving null controls, and leave-one-family-out validation on external labels. Raw correlations are disallowed.

failed_jumps.attempt: Map harmonic consonance and spectral intervals to band coherence.
failed_jumps.failure_reason: It generated an analogy to eigenfrequencies but no stricter residual benchmark than graph spectral reliability.

failed_jumps.attempt: Map amorphous backbone stability to tension/compression load paths.
failed_jumps.failure_reason: It supports intuition about load-bearing bridges but lacks a direct LP29 external label path beyond the network reliability version.

next_plan: Implement the synthetic benchmark as a small reproducible script and same-sample table schema; then run the benchmark in A-null and B-positive modes before touching real material labels. The next empirical step is to assemble external Hall/Drude/Wannier/spectral labels with provenance flags and forbid graph-generated labels as validation.

claims.statement: A scalar orbital-overlap budget is not a sufficient statistic for weighted graph connectivity because edge rearrangements can preserve the overlap budget while changing lambda_2, spectral radius, and targeted-damage response.

equations.label: F1
equations.description: orbital-overlap scalar budget S = sum w_ij

limits.expected: S unchanged while lambda_2 may change
limits.desc: non-equivalence of scalar budget and graph organization

equations.label: F2
equations.description: second eigenvalue of weighted or normalized Laplacian fixed by predeclared convention

assumptions: The baseline uses scalar or low-dimensional overlap controls, not the full weighted operator.
Graph weights are computed from structure before target labels.
Laplacian normalization is locked before evaluation.

claims.statement: High-betweenness damage is the sharpest residual probe because it asks whether defects on backbone bridges matter more than matched random defects after the same overlap penalty is controlled.

equations.label: F3
equations.description: targeted-minus-random damage gap at matched deleted weight or edge count

variables.D_random: mean loss under matched random edge removal

assumptions: Targeted and random attacks are matched by removed total weight or edge count.
Damage is evaluated on predeclared graph metrics and then tested against external residual labels.
Graph-Hamiltonian labels are diagnostic only and cannot validate material claims.

claims.statement: The decisive LP29-C2 test is external-label residual prediction after orbital-overlap and mobility-edge controls, not raw correlation between graph metrics and transport.

equations.label: F4
equations.description: Yp = (I - P_B) * Y_external, the external label residual after baseline projection

equations.label: F5
equations.description: Mp = (I - P_B) * M_graph, the graph metric residual after baseline projection

assumptions: External labels are not generated from the tested graph proxy.
Baseline controls include orbital overlap, onsite variance, density, mobility-edge margin, finite size, and batch.
Held-out prediction and null controls are reported even if negative.
